questions.question_text: When overtaking a cyclist, how much space should you provide?
options: Just enough to pass safely
As much as you would give a car
At least 1.5 meters
You should not overtake cyclists
questions.explanation: Providing extra space ensures that if a cyclist wobbles or avoids a road defect, they are still safe.

questions.question_text: How much space should you leave when overtaking a cyclist?
options: Only a few centimeters since they are small
The same space you would give to a car
As much space as you would give when overtaking a car
You should not overtake a cyclist under any circumstances
questions.explanation: Cyclists are vulnerable; you must allow them plenty of room to ensure their safety, as they may need to swerve to avoid obstacles.

questions.question_text: What is the most common cause of accidents at junctions?
options: Failure to look properly
Driving too slowly
Using a hands-free phone
Having high-beam headlights on
questions.explanation: Many accidents at junctions occur because drivers do not check their mirrors or surroundings carefully enough before proceeding.

questions.question_text: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, what should you do?
options: Speed up to clear the crossing
Slow down and be ready to stop
Flash your lights to tell them to cross
Drive around them if they are slow
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have priority at crossings, and you must always be prepared to stop for them.

questions.question_text: Which of these are most likely to be affected by strong side winds?
options: Motorcyclists
Heavy lorries
Four-wheel drive vehicles
Newer cars
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are light and unstable compared to cars, making them highly susceptible to being blown off-course by strong winds.

questions.question_text: What should you do when approaching a horse being ridden on the road?
options: Sound your horn to warn the rider
Pass slowly and leave plenty of room
Maintain your speed and drive past closely
Rev your engine to let them know you are there
questions.explanation: Horses are easily startled; passing slowly and quietly minimizes the risk of the horse panicking.

questions.question_text: When a school bus is dropping off children, what should you do?
options: Overtake as quickly as possible
Be prepared for children to step out suddenly
Keep your speed consistent
Flash your lights to warn the bus driver
questions.explanation: Children may be excited or unaware of traffic and can unexpectedly cross the road near buses.

questions.question_text: What does a flashing amber light on a school bus indicate?
options: The bus is turning left
The bus is warning that children are getting on or off
The bus has a mechanical fault
The bus is parked on a clearway
questions.explanation: This light serves as a specific warning to other road users to proceed with extra caution near the bus.

questions.question_text: Why should you be extra careful around elderly pedestrians?
options: They always walk on the road
They may have slower reactions or hearing
They do not know traffic rules
They are usually carrying heavy items
questions.explanation: Older road users might take longer to cross or be less able to judge traffic speed, requiring you to show patience.

questions.question_text: When you see a pedestrian standing on a traffic island, what should you expect?
options: They will definitely wait for you to pass
They might suddenly step into the road
They are just waiting for a friend
They will always face away from traffic
questions.explanation: Always be cautious around pedestrians, as they can behave unpredictably near traffic.

questions.question_text: Why must you allow extra room when passing a cyclist?
options: Because they travel faster than you
To avoid hitting them if they swerve or wobble
To show them the right of way
To comply with noise regulations
questions.explanation: Cyclists are vulnerable; leaving plenty of space provides a buffer if they need to avoid an obstacle.
